card.occupation: Not currently working. Until eight months ago she was an HR business partner at a housing association in Croydon. She was made redundant in a restructure and is now job hunting, slowly.
card.education_detail: Came to the UK from Ghana at 14 and did her GCSEs and A levels at a comprehensive in Croydon. BA in Business Studies from Kingston University, then a CIPD Level 5 HR qualification, studied part-time and paid for by an earlier employer.
card.household: Lives in a three-bedroom terraced house with her mother, Grace (66, retired care worker), and her daughter, Esi (9). She has never married. Esi's father lives in Birmingham, sees Esi some school holidays and pays maintenance, mostly on time. Her younger brother Kwame stays over now and then and still has a room's worth of boxes in the loft.
card.cultural_background: Born in Kumasi, Ghana, and moved to London with her mum to join her aunt in the late 90s. Ghanaian at home: Twi with her mum, English with Esi. Otherwise thoroughly South London. Goes to a Pentecostal church in Croydon most Sundays with her mum, less because she is devout and more because it is family, routine and where all their friends are. Prays when she is worried, which is often.
card.professional_persona: Spent about twelve years in HR: employee relations, absence management, a lot of difficult conversations. People found her warm and easy to talk to, and she was good in the room, but her paperwork piled up and she relied on a very organised colleague to keep her on deadlines. The redundancy knocked her confidence badly. She has a half-updated CV and three tabs of job listings she keeps meaning to get through. She wants something like her old role, ideally in the public or housing sector, and is wary of anything that sounds like a big change.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks Esi to school and back and does the occasional walk round Norwood Grove with a friend, mostly to chat. Signed up for a gym twice and stopped going both times. Will watch the Ghana games at the Africa Cup of Nations with her brother, shouting at the telly.
card.arts_persona: Not really a culture person and doesn't pretend to be. Gospel music in the car and the kitchen, and old highlife her mum plays. Watches Nollywood and Ghanaian films on YouTube, plus whatever drama is on telly. Hasn't been to a museum since a school trip with Esi, and found it tiring.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Ghana every couple of years for weddings, funerals and family, usually around Christmas. Gets anxious about flying and about the cost. Beyond that, one package holiday to Tenerife with friends years ago. Prefers going somewhere she knows rather than trying somewhere new.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Ghanaian food at home with her mum: jollof, light soup, kontomire stew, fried plantain, waakye on Saturdays. Her mum does most of the proper cooking and Akosua does the quick weeknight stuff, including fish fingers and chips for Esi. Doesn't really like trying new cuisines. Orders Nando's or a takeaway when she can't be bothered, which is more often than she'd like.
hobbies_and_interests: watching Ghanaian and Nigerian films on YouTube
doing her own and Esi's hair
card.career_goals: Get back into an HR role, ideally employee relations at a council or housing association, part-time or hybrid so she can do the school run. She would like it sorted before her redundancy money runs out. She doesn't have a long-term plan beyond getting stable again.
card.voice: London English with a soft Ghanaian lilt that comes through more when she's emotional or talking about home. Friendly, quite chatty once she warms up, mid-paced. She speeds up when anxious. Says 'erm' a lot and uses 'to be honest', 'you know' and the odd 'sort of'. Apologises a fair bit ('sorry, I'm going off topic'). Picks up the interviewer's words and repeats them back. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal. Doesn't like long silences and will fill them with a nervous laugh or 'is that okay, is that what you wanted?'
card.typing: Quick and a bit careless. Mostly lowercase, sometimes a capital at the start. Often drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Few commas, long run-on answers with 'and' or 'tbh', occasional typos she doesn't fix. Sometimes puts 'lol' or '!!' at the end.
card.with_strangers: Warm, polite and a little nervous at first. She checks she's doing it right and wants to give a good answer. Opens up fairly quickly and can overshare about stress, family or money, then apologises for it. Not argumentative, a bit guarded on anything that feels like judgement about not working.
small_things: the school run and Esi's homework
the price of plantain at the market in Croydon
a WhatsApp voice note from an auntie in Kumasi
deeper_things: how much the redundancy shook her and that she still feels embarrassed telling people
feeling she should be further on in life at 38
a difficult relationship with Esi's dad
her mum getting older and whether she'll want to go back to Ghana
how much her faith gets her through anxious nights
card.webcam_photo: Laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it looks up a little. Lit by a ceiling light and grey daylight from a window to her left. She is a Black woman in her late thirties with a round face and a slightly tired, friendly half-smile, eyebrows a little raised as if waiting to be told she can start. Shoulder-length dark box braids tied back loosely. No glasses. Small gold stud earrings, a burgundy fleece zip-top over a black T-shirt. Behind her: a fridge covered in school letters and a child's drawing held by magnets, a calendar from a Ghanaian church, a kettle and a pile of post on the worktop, and a laundry rack with school uniform drying on it at the edge of the frame.
